newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian steel plant to launch corporate bonds.
newsitem.headline: Romanian steel plant to launch corporate bonds.

text.p: Romanian state-run steel plant Siderca SA will launch the country's first corporate bonds next week to raise 7.0 billion lei to complete investment projects, a broker who manages the issue said on Thursday.
Subscription for the 350,000 domestic bonds with a nominal value of 20,000 lei each will start next Monday, Dana Tincu from Sita Finance SA securities company said.
Sita Finance leads a syndicate of 15 brokers handling the issue, whose subscription closes early next February.
The three-year bonds will be offered at a discount at 18,000 lei each, Tincu said. The annual coupon is 53 percent with a yield of 63.5 percent, she added.
After three years, Siderca will either buy the bonds back at their nominal value or allow their convertion into shares offering four shares per bond, Tincu said.
Siderca will use the money to complete a railway track manufacturing plant project which is intended to upgrade Romania's dilapidated railway network.
The company has contracts with the national railway company SNCFR on annual deliveries of 100,000 tonnes of track.
As foreign investors have shown interest in Siderca bonds, the company is contemplating the possibility of launching international corporate bonds in the near future, Tincu said.
The plant, based in the southeastern town of Calarasi and one of Romania's major producers of pig iron and steel, has an equity capital of 636.2 billion lei.
